title: No controversy over whether the blessed deserve some honor
source_text: LI. Porro ex iis quae hactenus thesibus hisce & superioribus exposita fuerunt, manifestum est nullam hic esse controversiam, An Beati tum homines, tum Angeli aliquo cultu & honore digni sint, & a nobis afficiendi: id enim ultro fatentur & docent Scholae Reformatae Doctores, nec contrarium, nisi per calumniam, ipsis imputari potest.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from those things which have so far been set out in these and the preceding theses, it is manifest that there is no controversy here, Whether the Blessed, both men and Angels, are worthy of some worship and honor, and are to be treated so by us: for this the Doctors of the Reformed School freely confess and teach, nor can the contrary be imputed to them except through calumny.
pass_b_english: From what these theses and the earlier ones have set out so far, it is clear that there is no dispute here over whether the blessed, both men and angels, deserve some kind of reverence and honor and ought to receive it from us. The teachers of the Reformed school readily admit and teach this, and the contrary cannot be laid to their charge except by slander.

choices.why: Here cultus is the broad honor both sides grant, not religious worship; 'reverence' avoids implying latria.
